questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the compounds of List-I with their effects in List-II:
List-IList-II
(a)Chloramphenicol(i)Malaria
(b)Thyroxine(ii)Anaesthetic
(c)Chloroquine(iii)Goiter
(d)Chloroform(iv)Typhoid fever
questions.solution:
Chloramphenicol is a broad-spectrum antibiotic which is highly effective in the treatment of typhoid fever.

Thyroxine is an iodine-containing hormone secreted by the thyroid gland. Its deficiency causes goiter.

Chloroquine is a widely used antimalarial drug used for the treatment and prevention of malaria.

Chloroform is a volatile liquid that was historically used as a general anaesthetic in surgery.

Thus, the correct matching is (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

Answer: a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is a non-narcotic analgesic?
questions.solution:
Aspirin in classified as a non-narcotic
analgesic because it does not produce the typical effects associated with narcotic or opiod analgesics. In addition to its analgesic effects, it also possesses anti-inflammatory and antipyretic (fever reducing) properties.
It is commonly used for relieving mild to moderate pain, reducing inflammation, headaches etc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reaction has both \(\Delta $\mathrm{H}$\) and \(\Delta $\mathrm{S}$\) - ve. The rate of reaction
options: remains unaffected by change in temperature
cannot be predicted for change in temperature
questions.solution:
The reaction is thermodynamic ally favored when \(\Delta G < 0 \)
\[ $\begin{array}{l}\Delta$ G=\Delta$ H-T $\Delta$ S \\ $\Delta$ G=-v e-T(-v e) \\ $\Delta$ G=-v e+T(+v e) \end{array} \]
Therefore, on increasing the temperature \(\Delta \mathrm{G}\) becomes positive (+ve). Hence, the rate of reaction increases with
decrease in temperature.$

questions.q: The statement that is NOT correct is
options: Lactose has glycosidic linkage between \( C_{4} \) of glucose and \( C_{1} \) of galactose unit.
Aldose or ketose sugars in alkaline medium do not isomerism.
Pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine.
questions.solution:
Aldose or ketose sugars in alkaline medium isomerize. For example; on heating with conc. solution of \( $\mathrm{NaOH}$\) glucose
(aldose) first turns yellow and then brown and finally resinifies with dilute solution of \( $\mathrm{NaOH}$\) glucose (aldose) undergoes a
reversible isomerization and is converted into a mixture of D-glucose, D-maltose and D-fructose. This reaction is known
as lobry de Bruyn-van Ekenstein rearrangement.

The facts which are solids at ordinary temperatures, contain a large proportion of saturated acids, like-myristic acid, palmitic acid, stearic acid. e.g., glyceryl trioleate, which contains unsaturated acids components is an oil. Glyceryl tristearate which contains only saturated acids component is a fat.
